executive_assessment.text: Mapped fluvial hazards around Mansa Konko, Kuntaur and Janjanbureh differ from modeled coastal/heat scenarios and the dated 2022 West Coast/Greater Banjul flood accounts.
Decentralized DRM functionality and logistics/staffing constraints shape capacity; aid-allocation tensions do not establish climate-related violence.

geographic_notes.text: Source dated 2023-11 reports: For the 2022 extreme-rain event, parts of West Coast Region received 276 mm in 20 hours; policy cites a separate World Bank estimate of 80,000 affected in Greater Banjul.
Source dated 2026-03-15 reports: Middle-river floodplains around Mansa Konko, Kuntaur and Janjanbureh have the assessment's highest fluvial hazard.
Source dated 2026-03-15 reports: Current modeled coastal flooding inundates low-lying Tanbi Wetland west of Banjul; the report says its mangroves attenuate flooding inland.
Source dated 2026-03-15 reports: Under future extreme coastal-flood scenarios, Banjul and Brikama show substantial increases in modeled flood depth compared with current conditions.

known_gaps.text: Automated machine-screening is not independent source verification or human approval. 18 of 18 evidence records and 1 of 1 pathways lack claim-level verification in this remediation; review the linked records before relying on them.
No independent post-event validation of the 2022 flood impact counts was inspected.
The CCDR's qualitative climate–conflict pathway is not a causal estimate and does not quantify conflict incidence.
Draft collection pending human source review and approval. IDA eligibility is not an FCV classification.
National and selected local examples do not establish district-level coverage or causal attribution.
The official IOM DTM climate-vulnerability assessment page returned HTTP 403; no claims use search-indexed or secondary text.
The inspected sources report climate exposure, migration pressure and aid-delivery tensions, but do not establish climate-related violence or conflict disrupting adaptation delivery.
The GCA assessment models climate hazards and infrastructure exposure; it does not estimate household vulnerability, conflict outcomes or adaptation delivered.
NDMA's cited 80,000 Greater Banjul estimate comes from a separate 2022 World Bank remote assessment and should not be combined with OCHA rapid-needs totals.
